goal: Try both scientifically different operation orders using real PRISM maximum temperature
command: from cubedynamics import data,pipe,verbs as v; import json; cube=data.temperature(source="prism",statistic="maximum",bbox=[-105.30,39.95,-105.20,40.05],start="2024-01-01",end="2024-01-10"); a=pipe(cube)|v.threshold_state(threshold=5.0,direction="above",name="warm_day")|v.mean(over="time",keep_dim=False); b=pipe(cube)|v.mean(over="time",keep_dim=False)|v.threshold_state(threshold=5.0,direction="above",name="warm_mean"); print("A_DATA",a.unwrap()); print("A_STATE",json.dumps(a.semantic_state.as_dict(),default=str,sort_keys=True)); print("A_TRACE",json.dumps([s.as_dict() for s in a.semantic_trace],default=str,sort_keys=True)); print("A_EXPLAIN",a.explain()); print("A_VALIDATE",a.validate()); print("B_DATA",b.unwrap()); print("B_STATE",json.dumps(b.semantic_state.as_dict(),default=str,sort_keys=True)); print("B_TRACE",json.dumps([s.as_dict() for s in b.semantic_trace],default=str,sort_keys=True)); print("B_EXPLAIN",b.explain()); print("B_VALIDATE",b.validate())
expected_behavior: Both threshold then mean and mean then threshold are expressible, produce visibly different result meanings, and preserve ordered inspectable traces
